basicPropertyValues.val: 8/17/09: specified inputs of one process are not necessarily specified inputs of a larger process that it is part of. This is in contrast to how 'has participant' works.

definition.val: The inverse property of is specified output of

A relation between a completely executed planned process and a continuant participating in that process. The presence of the continuant at the end of the process is explicitly specified in the objective specification which the process realizes the concretization of.
a relation between a continuant and a process, in which the continuant is somehow involved in the process

A relationship between a generically dependent continuant and a specifically dependent continuant or process, in which the generically dependent continuant depends on some independent continuant or process in virtue of the fact that the specifically dependent continuant or process also depends on that same independent continuant. A generically dependent continuant may be concretized as multiple specifically dependent continuants or processes.
a relation between an independent continuant (the bearer) and a quality, in which the quality specifically depends on the bearer for its existence

basicPropertyValues.val: A bearer can have many qualities, and its qualities can exist for different periods of time, but none of its qualities can exist when the bearer does not exist.

definition.val: p has input c iff: p is a process, c is a material entity, c is a participant in p, c is present at the start of p, and the state of c is modified during p.

comments: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002233

definition.val: p has output c iff c is a participant in p, c is present at the end of p, and c is not present in the same state at the beginning of p.

A relation that groups properties quantifying the chemical composition of a molecular system, such as the total number of atoms, residues and molecules of each type. Those counts give the stoichiometry and the overall size of the system being simulated. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that gives the total number of atoms in a molecular system, counting every molecule present including solvent and ions. It is the single figure that most determines what a simulation will cost, because the work of each step grows with it. A solvated protein system is usually tens of thousands of atoms, most of them water. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NATOM pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different atom types the force field uses for a system, rather than the number of atoms. An atom type is a category such as an aromatic carbon or a carbonyl oxygen, and every atom of that type shares the same interaction parameters. The figure reflects how chemically varied the system is. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NTYPES pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the total number of residues in a molecular system, a residue being 1 building block of a polymer, such as an amino acid, or a small whole molecule, such as water or an ion. In a system with explicit solvent most residues are usually water molecules, so the figure grows with the amount of solvent. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NRES pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of the last residue treated as part of the solute, which fixes where the receptor ends. Everything numbered beyond it is ligand, solvent or ions. The boundary matters because analyses of binding must know which atoms belong to the receptor. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The IPTRES pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of ligand molecules in a molecular system. A ligand here is a small molecule being studied for how it binds to a larger one. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that gives the number of ligand molecules in a system that carry a net electrical charge. It matters because charged ligands change how the system must be neutralised and how its electrostatics behave. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that gives the number of distinct shapes of a ligand being considered in a study. Docking and conformational analysis generate many shapes of the same molecule, and how many were kept affects what the result means. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total atoms in the largest residue

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atoms in the biggest single residue of a system. A standard amino acid has fewer than 30, so a much larger figure marks something else, such as a cofactor, a ligand, a lipid or a modified residue. It is a quick way to notice that a system contains something other than a plain polymer. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NMXRS pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of massless interaction sites in a molecular model, which carry charge or interaction parameters but sit at no nucleus. They let charge be placed where no atom is, such as on a lone pair of electrons or slightly off an oxygen. Water models with 4 sites and some halogen bonding parameters are the usual reason a system has any. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMEXTRA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties quantifying the covalent structure and connectivity of a molecular system, such as the number of bonds, angles and dihedral angles. Together they describe the topology, which is the graph of how the atoms are joined. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds in a system in which at least 1 of the 2 atoms is a hydrogen. These bonds vibrate faster than anything else in the system, so they are usually held at a fixed length to permit a longer timestep. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NBONH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds in a system that join 2 heavy atoms, with no hydrogen involved. These bonds form the skeleton of each molecule and are not normally constrained, because they vibrate slowly enough for the timestep to follow them. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MBONA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in a system in which at least one of the 3 atoms is a hydrogen. Angles involving hydrogen bend fastest, so some simulations constrain them as well as the bonds. Doing so permits a longer timestep still, at the cost of losing that motion. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NTHETH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in a system formed entirely by heavy atoms, that is atoms other than hydrogen. These angles set the shape of each molecule's skeleton and are almost never constrained. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MTHETA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedral angles with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in a system in which at least 1 of the 4 defining atoms is a hydrogen. A dihedral angle describes a twist defined by 4 atoms. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPHIH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedral angles without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in a system defined entirely by heavy atoms, that is atoms other than hydrogen. They include the backbone dihedral angles of a protein, which largely control the shapes its chain can adopt. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MPHIA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total excluded atom pairs

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atom pairs whose ordinary non-bonded interaction is deliberately left out of the calculation. Pairs joined through a bond, an angle or a dihedral are excluded because the bonded terms already describe how they interact, and in most force fields the pairs 3 bonds apart are then added back at reduced strength. The exclusion list is part of the topology rather than a setting. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NNB pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting the degrees of freedom held fixed during a simulation, such as the bonds and angles made rigid by an algorithm like SHAKE. They record how far the natural dynamics of the system has been altered. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds whose length is held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Each constrained bond removes 1 degree of freedom from the system, which is why the figure is needed to compute temperature correctly. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NBONA - MBONA

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Constraining angles as well as bonds permits a longer timestep but removes the motion being constrained. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NTHETA - MTHETA

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedrals with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Constraining a dihedral prevents a rotation entirely, so it is done rarely and deliberately. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NPHIA - MPHIA

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting the distinct force field parameters applied to a molecular system, such as the number of unique bond, angle and atom types. The counts indicate how complex the energy function used to model the system is. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total unique bond types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different bond parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Two bonds share a type when the force field gives them the same preferred length and stiffness. The figure reflects how chemically varied the bonding in the system is, not how many bonds there are. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMBND pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total unique angle types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different angle parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Two angles share a type when the force field gives them the same preferred value and stiffness. The figure reflects the variety of local geometries the system contains. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMANG pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total unique dihedral types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different dihedral parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Dihedral parameters control which rotations are preferred, so this figure reflects how varied the conformational behaviour of the system is. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPTRA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total atom types in the parameter file

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atom types defined in the force field parameter files being used, rather than the number appearing in a single system. It describes the coverage of the force field itself. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NATYP pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total distinct hydrogen bond pair types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of distinct pair types for the 10-12 hydrogen bond potential, an older treatment that gives hydrogen bonds an energy term of their own. Modern force fields describe hydrogen bonds through ordinary electrostatics and van der Waals terms instead, so this figure is 0 for most current systems. A non-zero value marks an older parameter set. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPHB pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting what a chemical transformation in a free energy calculation covers, such as the atoms, bonds and angles being changed during the simulation. They set out the scope of the alchemical modification performed. (UNVERIFIED)
In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of bonds being chemically transformed.

comments: The NBPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of angles being chemically transformed.

comments: The NGPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of dihedrals being chemically transformed.

comments: The NDPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with all atoms in the perturbed group

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bonds in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 2 atoms both lie in the group being transformed. An alchemical calculation changes 1 chemical group into another in small steps, to compute the free energy difference between them. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MBPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with all atoms in perturbed groups

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 3 atoms all lie in the group being transformed. An alchemical calculation changes 1 chemical group into another in small steps, to compute the free energy difference between them. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MGPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedrals with all atoms in perturbed groups

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 4 atoms all lie in the group being transformed. An alchemical calculation changes 1 chemical group into another in small steps, to compute the free energy difference between them. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MDPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties describing the overall state or the main qualitative features of a molecular system, such as yes-or-no flags and short textual descriptions of its composition and setup. They give high-level context about what kind of simulation it is. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a molecular system contains at least 1 ligand molecule. It marks at a glance which simulations concern binding rather than a molecule on its own. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether salt ions were added to a system beyond the counterions needed to make it neutral. Added salt sets the ionic strength, which changes how strongly charges are screened and how molecules interact. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A boolean descriptor indicating whether the molecular system houses an explicit lipid bilayer, rather than just an aqueous or implicit solvent environment. This is a higher-level descriptor not directly present in the prmtop pointers.

A relation that states whether the starting structure contained more than one arrangement for some part of the molecule. Crystal structures often record 2 positions for a flexible side chain, and which was used changes what the simulation began from. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A textual description of the types, proportions and spatial arrangements of different lipid molecules used to construct a biological membrane. This is a higher-level descriptor not directly present in the prmtop pointers.

A numerical or string representation of the relative amounts of different lipid types in a membrane. For example, a value of "3:1" could describe a mixture of two different lipids. This provides a semiquantitative description of the membrane composition.

A relation that associates a molecular system with the index of the first solvent molecule in its ordered list of molecules. Molecules before it make up the solute, and molecules from it onwards make up the solvent. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with how many solvent molecules it contains. It quantifies the amount of solvent used to solvate the solute. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a trajectory with the atom count recorded in each of its frames. It reflects the size of the coordinate set stored at every saved time point. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a mapping from ion species to the count of ions of each species present. It records the ionic composition used, for example, to neutralize charge or set ionic strength.

comments: This property stores its value as text, not as a number. The text lists each kind of ion and how many of them there are, for example {"Na+": 12, "Cl-": 10}. That is how the simulation files themselves write it. The other count properties next to this one use plain numbers, because each of them counts a single thing. This one has to count several kinds of ion at the same time, and the ontology has no way yet to say which count belongs to which ion. We looked at two other ways of doing it: making a separate property for every kind of ion, or making a small object that holds one ion and its number. Both would add a lot of work for little gain right now, so we kept the text form. The text itself can be checked later with SHACL, a rule language for checking data files.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular system with how many bond-angle terms are defined in its force-field topology. It helps describe the size and complexity of the bonded interaction set. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with how many dihedral, or torsion, terms are defined in its force-field topology. It helps describe the size and complexity of the bonded interaction set. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation with how many times a geometric constraint algorithm, such as SHAKE, failed to converge during the run. A nonzero value can signal instability in the integration. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation run with an indication of whether it finished normally or terminated abnormally. It supports quick screening of runs for successful completion. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that indicates whether a run was started as a continuation of a previous run rather than from initial conditions. It distinguishes restarted runs from fresh ones. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether the atomic coordinates in a trajectory have been translated back into the primary periodic unit cell. It records whether periodic-image wrapping was applied to the stored coordinates. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a simulation uses a combined quantum-mechanics and molecular-mechanics treatment for part of the system. It records whether a region is described at the quantum level while the remainder uses a classical force field. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that allows the software to apply a time-averaged or spatial-averaged guiding force derived from the system's own trajectory to accelerate low-frequency, concerted motions and enhance conformational sampling.
A relation that controls whether a spherical portion of solvent (water) is applied around a solute, restrained by a soft half-harmonic potential.
A relation that indicates whether periodic box dimension information is present for a molecular system or trajectory. It records whether unit-cell size and shape data are available. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that indicates whether atomic velocity data are stored alongside coordinates in a file or trajectory. Velocities are needed to continue a run exactly from where it stopped. (UNVERIFIED)
OBSOLETE. A relation that records the kind of periodic box used for a molecular system, such as rectangular or truncated octahedral. It identifies the geometry of the periodic unit cell.

comments: Retired 2026-08-13. It duplicated MOLSIM:000297 has periodic box type, which links a molecular simulation system to the class MOLSIM:000032 box type and its five children. This term held the same information as a plain string, so no value could be checked, while the object property points at a real hierarchy that a reasoner can use. Its label also broke the house convention: ten of the eleven data properties ending in flag are yes-or-no values, and this one recorded which box geometry was used.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties describing a molecular dynamics trajectory as a whole, such as how many frames it holds and the format its coordinates are stored in. (UNVERIFIED)

basicPropertyValues.val: Domain chosen 2026-08-13. This domain asserts something the other grouping properties here do not: anything carrying a child of this property, such as MOLSIM:002138 number of frames, is inferred to be a MOLSIM:001081 simulation trajectory. That is correct if a frame count is only ever recorded about a trajectory. If the source metadata ever records a frame count against a whole run rather than against its trajectory file, the domain should be MOLSIM:000000 molecular dynamics process instead. Confirm against the MDDB records before relying on it.

definition.val: A relation that associates a trajectory with how many saved frames it contains. It reflects how many time points were recorded over the course of the run. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a trajectory or coordinate file with an identifier of the file format used to store its coordinates. It records how the coordinate data are encoded, for example as NetCDF or formatted text. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties whose values are ordered lists of numbers describing the size and shape of the periodic simulation box of a molecular system, such as its edge lengths and angles. Each list is stored as text. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with an array giving the lengths and angles that define its periodic simulation box. It captures the full geometry of the periodic unit cell. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with an array giving the periodic box lengths and angles at the start of a run. It records the initial unit-cell geometry before any volume changes. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that groups properties recording the names and labels assigned to components of a molecular system, such as residue and atom-type names. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the residue name used to identify its solvent in the topology, such as WAT for water. It records the label under which solvent is stored. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the ordered list of residue names for its constituent residues. It records the per-residue naming as given in the system's topology. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the set of distinct residue names it contains. It summarizes the kinds of residues present without regard to how many times each occurs. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the set of distinct force-field atom types it uses. It summarizes the range of parameterized atom types present in the topology. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the identifier of the intrinsic radii set used in a generalized Born implicit-solvent calculation. It records which parameterization defines the atomic solvation radii. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties recording what a simulation or a checking step reported about itself, such as an error message, a warning, or the outcome of a validation check. It gathers the output a run produced about its own progress, as distinct from the settings it was given. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation or processing step with textual diagnostic output emitted when a fault occurred. It captures the message describing why a run failed. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation or processing step with a textual warning emitted during execution. Such warnings flag potential problems that did not necessarily stop the run. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with a non-fatal issue raised during a validation check. It flags a concern found while verifying correctness or consistency. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with a fault raised during a validation check that caused the check to fail. It records a validation failure. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with the outcome of a check verifying that its data are mutually consistent. It records whether internal consistency tests passed or failed. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory or restart file contains atomic coordinate data. Almost every trajectory does, but a file holding only velocities or only forces does not, and reading one expecting coordinates fails. The flag lets a tool decide what a file is good for before opening it. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory or restart file contains per-atom force data. Forces are written less often than coordinates, because they add to the size of a trajectory and are needed only for some uses, such as force analysis or training machine-learning models. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory file contains per-frame time-stamp data. Without it the frames have an order but no times, so any quantity involving a rate has to assume the interval between them. Stored times also reveal a gap where frames were lost. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a simulation applies NMR-derived restraints or dynamically varying conditions. Such restraints pull the system towards experimental measurements, so the resulting structures reflect the data as well as the force field. A trajectory produced this way must not be treated as a free simulation. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether metadata extraction ran in a degraded mode because one or more input files were missing or unreadable. A record produced this way is incomplete rather than wrong, and the missing fields are absent rather than zero. Marking it prevents a partial record being read as a complete one. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying target-temperature schedule. A run that heats or cools during its course is not described by a single temperature, so any average taken across it would be meaningless. The flag warns that the run is not at a steady state.

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying positional-restraint weight schedule. Restraints are commonly released gradually while a system settles, so the strength recorded at the start does not describe the whole run. The flag marks a run in which the restraints changed. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying non-bonded cutoff schedule. Changing the cutoff during a run changes how much of each interaction is included, so energies from different parts of the trajectory are not comparable. It is unusual, which is why it is worth recording when it happens. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a descriptive feature or heuristic modification of its force field, such as CMAP terms, which correct backbone dihedral energies, or conversion from CHARMM to AMBER format by the CHAMBER tool. These details are not conveyed by the name of the force field, so recording them keeps the force field identifiable from the metadata alone. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a serialized mapping from each residue type to the number of residues of that type present. It says what the system is made of in one value, without a separate term for every residue type. It is stored as text because the set of residue types is open-ended. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation with the complete, serialized set of key-value control parameters parsed from its input file. It keeps every setting as written, so nothing in the original input is lost. It is a record for a person to read rather than a structure for a machine to reason over. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that determines specialized algorithmic modifications designed to bypass the steep computational cost of standard REMD by applying enhanced sampling to only a specific subsystem or localized region.

A relation that associates a simulation stage with the file path or identifier of the restart file used to initiate it. It is what connects one stage to the one before it, so a chain of stages can be reconstructed after the fact. Without it the stages of a long run are a set of files in no particular order. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether the total electrostatic charge of a molecular system is effectively zero, that is, whether the system is electrically neutral. A charged periodic system interacts with its own images in a way that distorts energies, so counter-ions are normally added to neutralise it. A system reported as not neutral needs that explained. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a short human-readable summary of the hydrogen masses observed, such as the mass range and the count of hydrogen atoms, used to describe hydrogen mass repartitioning. Repartitioning moves mass from heavy atoms onto the hydrogens bonded to them, which slows the fastest vibrations and permits a longer timestep. The summary shows at a glance whether it was applied and how far. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a graphics processing unit with the model name of the specific device used to run a simulation, such as the name reported by the CUDA runtime. Recording the device helps explain the speed of a run and makes it possible to repeat the run on the same hardware. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether hydrogen mass repartitioning was inferred from the integration timestep, specifically a timestep of 3 femtoseconds or larger, rather than detected directly from the hydrogen masses in the topology. The inference is a reasonable guess and not a reading, because such a timestep is otherwise unstable.

A relation that associates a simulation protocol with the total number of integration steps performed across all of its stages. When every stage uses the same timestep, multiplying the 2 gives the total simulated time. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its proteins. Proteins are the large chain-like molecules built from amino acids; this reports how many atoms make up all of them together. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its nucleic acids, that is DNA and RNA taken together. It separates the nucleic acid part of a system from protein, solvent and ions in a single figure. A value of 0 marks a system with no nucleic acid at all. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its lipids. Lipids are the fatty molecules that form cell membranes. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to ions. In most simulations these ions are single charged atoms, such as sodium or chloride, added to balance the charge or set the salt concentration. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its solvent, which is usually water. It counts atoms, not whole solvent molecules. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms that fall into none of the named categories (protein, nucleic acid, lipid, ion, solvent). It captures leftovers such as small-molecule ligands or cofactors. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of residues in its proteins. A residue is one amino-acid building block of a protein chain. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of residues in its nucleic acids. Here a residue is one nucleotide building block of a DNA or RNA chain. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of lipid residues it contains. Some force fields write each lipid molecule as 1 residue, while others, such as the AMBER LIPID21 force field, split it into a head group residue and separate tail residues, so this figure need not equal the number of lipid molecules. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with how many nucleosomes it contains. A nucleosome is the basic repeating unit of chromatin, a stretch of DNA wound around a core of histone proteins. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of nucleotides per DNA strand

definition.val: A relation that associates the system with the length of a DNA strand, measured as the number of nucleotide bases it contains. Because a system can contain several strands, this may be recorded once per strand. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with an ordered list of the 3 angles between the edges of its periodic simulation box, usually written α, β and γ. The list is stored as text, as read from or written to a simulation file. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a saved trajectory includes the atomic positions (the 3-D coordinates of every atom over time). Positions are the most basic trajectory data and are almost always present. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a saved trajectory includes the forces acting on each atom over time. Forces are optional extra data, useful for example when training machine-learning models. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records the version number of a piece of software, such as an MD engine, the program that runs the simulation (for example, version 2024.1). Recording the version helps make a simulation reproducible, because software behaviour can change between versions. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that records whether a simulated system includes an antibody, a Y-shaped immune protein that recognises and sticks to a specific target such as a virus. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether a simulated system includes a nanobody, a very small, single-piece version of an antibody, originally from animals such as llamas, used as a compact binding tool. A nanobody is a single antibody domain, roughly a tenth the size of a full antibody. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether the system includes a linker histone, such as histone H1, an extra histone that binds the DNA where it enters and leaves the nucleosome core. It is not part of the core of 8 histone proteins and is missing from many experimental structures, so its presence changes what a simulation represents. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether the histone proteins in a system still have their tails, the flexible ends that extend out from the nucleosome core and are often chemically modified to control gene activity. The tails have no fixed shape, so they are often removed from a model to make it easier to simulate, which also removes the parts that carry those chemical marks. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties recording what a simulation run was given to start from, such as the settings parsed from its input file or the restart file it continued from. It covers the input side of a run, as distinct from what the run reported about itself. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular dynamics process with the file path or identifier of the topology file defining the simulated system, such as an AMBER prmtop file or a GROMACS top file. The topology file states which atoms are present, how they are bonded, which parameters they were assigned, and which chemical states were assumed when the system was built. (UNVERIFIED)

basicPropertyValues.val: MOLSIM records the composition of a simulated system at the system level and points at the topology and coordinate files for the per-residue detail, rather than restating that detail term by term. This is why there is no vocabulary for individual histidine or cysteine states: those are decided per residue and per atom, and the topology file states them exactly. Paired with MOLSIM:002257 has coordinate file path, which records the starting positions.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular dynamics process with the file path or identifier of the coordinate file holding the starting position of every atom, such as an AMBER inpcrd or rst7 file or a GROMACS gro file. Together with the topology file it fixes the exact system state a run began from. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with any solvent added alongside water, such as urea, glycerol or an alcohol. A cosolvent changes how the solute behaves, and a record that omits it describes a different system from the one that was run. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because a system may contain more than 1 cosolvent and each may carry a concentration. Values look like "urea 8 M" or "glycerol 30 percent, DMSO 5 percent". Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

basicPropertyValues.val: Holds text rather than pointing at a named class for each substance, and that is a deliberate choice rather than a shortcut. Pointing at named classes would need MOLSIM classes for urea, glycerol, DMSO and every other cosolvent, which is a chemistry vocabulary that ChEBI already provides with roughly 190,000 terms. The ChEBI import was removed on 2026-08-24 because all 189 classes it delivered were unreferenced, and the agreed approach records what a system is made of at the system level while pointing at the topology file for the per-residue chemical detail. The cost of the text form is real: urea, Urea, URE and 8M urea are the same substance and different strings, so a search by substance is unreliable. Revisit only when a specific record must be queried by substance rather than read by a person. The fix then is to import the few named ChEBI terms actually needed, bounded so that no ancestors arrive with them, and change this property to point at those. The same reasoning applies to the data properties MOLSIM:001161 lipid composition and MOLSIM:001162 lipid ratio, which also hold text.

definition.val: A relation that records whether the 2 layers of a simulated membrane hold the same mixture of lipids as each other. Real cell membranes usually differ between their 2 sides, so whether a simulation copied that difference or ignored it changes what the results can be said to show. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with the size of its membrane patch in the plane of the membrane. The patch must be wide enough that a protein does not interact with its own periodic copy across the boundary, so the size limits which conclusions the simulation can support. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because the size has 2 numbers and a unit. Values look like "9.5 x 9.5 nm" or "120 x 95 angstrom". It carries no unit restriction for the same reason MOLSIM:001213 periodic box dimensions carries none: the unit and value pattern describes a single number, and a patch size is two. A single length in this domain does take that pattern, as MOLSIM:001875 membrane width does. Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with the rule used to delete lipids that overlapped the protein when the membrane was built. Placing a protein into a lipid patch always leaves some lipids sitting where the protein is, and the rule chosen for removing them decides how many lipids the finished system holds. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because the rule is usually a short description rather than a single number. Values look like "lipids with any atom within 0.6 nm of the protein were deleted" or "removed by the InflateGRO procedure". Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

definition.val: The term was initially used in an attempt to structure part of the ontology, but in retrospect failed to do a good job.
Class has all its metadata, but is either not guaranteed to be in its final location in the asserted IS_A hierarchy or refers to another class that is not complete.
The term was created to ease viewing/sorting terms for development purposes, but will not be included in a release.

Class has undergone final review, is ready for use, and will be included in the next release. Any class lacking "ready_for_release" should be considered likely to change place in hierarchy, have its definition refined, or be obsoleted in the next release.  Those classes deemed "ready_for_release" will also derived from a chain of ancestor classes that are also "ready_for_release."
Class is being worked on; however, the metadata (including definition) are not complete or sufficiently clear to the branch editors.
Nothing done yet beyond assigning a unique class ID and proposing a preferred term.
All definitions, placement in the asserted IS_A hierarchy and required minimal metadata are complete. The class is awaiting a final review by someone other than the term editor.
The term was created to temporarily stand in for a semantic purpose, but is no longer needed, typically due to another permanent term being defined.
The term has been combined with one or more other terms to create a more encompassing (merged) term.
The term has been replaced by a term imported from another ontology.
The term has been split into two or more new terms.

basicPropertyValues.val: A Formal Theory of Substances, Qualities, and Universals, http://ontology.buffalo.edu/bfo/SQU.pdf

definition.val: A defined class is a class that is defined by a set of logically necessary and sufficient conditions but is not a universal
A named class expression is a logical expression that is given a name. The name can be used in place of the expression.

nodes.lbl: to be replaced with external ontology term

definition.val: Terms with this status should eventually replaced with a term from another ontology.
A term that is metadata complete, has been reviewed, and problems have been identified that require discussion before release. Such a term requires editor note(s) to identify the outstanding issues.

A protein structural database that is the single worldwide archive for experimentally determined 3-dimensional structures of large biological molecules, including proteins, nucleic acids and their complexes. Many simulations of biological molecules begin with a structure taken from it. Its accession codes are the standard way a structure is cited. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein structural database that is the European member of the worldwide Protein Data Bank partnership, run by EMBL-EBI, holding the same archive and adding its own search and analysis tools. The members of the partnership share 1 set of entries, so a structure deposited through any of them appears at all. What differs is the interface and the services built on top. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein structural database that is the Japanese member, and a founding member, of the worldwide Protein Data Bank partnership, run at the Institute for Protein Research of Osaka University. It processes the structures deposited mainly from Asia and the Middle East, holds the same archive as the other members, and develops its own tools and services. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein structural database that gives a pictorial summary of each 3D structure in the Protein Data Bank, with schematic diagrams of molecular interactions, protein domains, ligand binding sites and other structural features. It helps a reader understand the contents of an entry quickly, without opening the coordinates. (UNVERIFIED)

The Nucleic Acid Database (NDB) was a specialized, value-added web repository founded in 1991 to collect, archive, and distribute three-dimensional (3D) structural information about DNA, RNA, and their protein/ligand complexes. The legacy NDB resource has been officially retired. It has been replaced by the Nucleic Acid Knowledgebase (NAKB), which preserves all original NDB functionality while expanding coverage to modern structural biology data.

The Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB) is a global public repository for 3D electron microscopy (3DEM) density maps and tomograms of biological specimens, macromolecules, viruses, and subcellular structures. It stores cryogenic-sample electron microscopy (cryoEM) volumes, helical reconstructions, electron tomograms, subtomogram averages, and electron crystallography maps.
An electron microscopy database storing the raw, 2D micrographs and tilt series that researchers use to build 3D cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps and models (which are archived in the EMDB).

A nucleic acid sequence database of the U.S. National Institutes of Health, maintained by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), that holds an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences. It is the American member of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration, together with ENA in Europe and DDBJ in Japan, and the 3 exchange records daily. (UNVERIFIED)

A knowledge-based database of protein sequences together with what is known about each protein's function, structure and modifications, run by the UniProt consortium. It was formed by joining Swiss-Prot, TrEMBL and the PIR Protein Sequence Database, and it has a manually reviewed section, Swiss-Prot, and a much larger automatically annotated section, TrEMBL. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid sequence database, run by EMBL-EBI, covering raw sequencing reads, assembled sequences and their annotations from organisms of every kind. It is the European member of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration, whose 3 members exchange records daily, so a sequence deposited at any of them can be found at all 3. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid sequence database that is the Japanese member of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration, together with GenBank in the United States and ENA in Europe. The 3 members exchange records daily, so a sequence deposited at any of them can be found at all 3. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein sequence database that forms the manually annotated and reviewed section of the UniProt Knowledgebase. Its entries combine the protein sequence with functional annotation and cross-references, checked by curators against the literature, which makes it the most reliable part of UniProtKB. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein sequence database that forms the automatically annotated, unreviewed section of the UniProt Knowledgebase. Most of its entries are translations of the coding sequences submitted to the nucleotide sequence databases, and together they give broad coverage of known proteins. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein sequence database, run by NCBI, that provides a curated, non-redundant set of reference protein sequences, often linked to the matching nucleotide sequences and genome annotations. Its records serve as stable reference points for identifying, annotating and comparing proteins. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein sequence database whose Protein Sequence Database was one of the first curated collections of protein sequences, growing out of an atlas of protein sequences begun in the 1960s. That collection was merged into the UniProt Knowledgebase, and the resource itself remains a member of the UniProt consortium. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid sequence database, run by NCBI, that provides a non-redundant, annotated set of reference sequences for chromosomes, genomic regions, transcripts and RNAs. Each sequence serves as a stable reference for the organism it comes from, which supports genome annotation. (UNVERIFIED)

A chemical structure database within PubChem, run by NCBI, that holds 1 record for each unique, validated small-molecule structure, derived from the substance records that many contributors deposit. Each record gives identifiers, computed properties and links to related information. (UNVERIFIED)

A chemical structure database and ontology covering small molecules that take part in biological processes, as products, reactants or regulators. Being an ontology as well as a dictionary, it records how compounds relate to one another rather than only listing them. (UNVERIFIED)

A chemical structure database of commercially available compounds, prepared in ready-to-dock 3D formats for virtual screening, which is the computer search for molecules that may bind a target. It is provided by the Irwin and Shoichet laboratories at the University of California, San Francisco, and holds hundreds of millions of purchasable compounds with annotated properties. (UNVERIFIED)

A drug information database holding detailed data on drugs together with their targets, interactions and metabolism. It combines information about each drug with information about the proteins it acts on, and its data are free for non-commercial research but need a licence for commercial use. (UNVERIFIED)

A chemical structure database, owned by the Royal Society of Chemistry, that gives free access to millions of chemical structures with their properties and related information, gathered from many sources. It can be searched by chemical name, synonym, trade name, registry number or structure. (UNVERIFIED)

A drug information database recording the protein and nucleic acid targets that drugs act on, the drugs directed at each, and the diseases involved. It is organised around the target rather than the compound. It is used to find what has already been tried against a protein before a new study is designed. (UNVERIFIED)

A drug information database, run by the U.S. National Library of Medicine, that publishes the labels of marketed drugs as submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, including package inserts. The labels describe each drug's ingredients, uses, dosage, warnings and side effects for healthcare providers and the public. (UNVERIFIED)

A bioactivity database of manually curated data on drug-like small molecules and their measured activity against biological targets, mostly proteins, maintained by EMBL-EBI. It brings together chemical, bioactivity and genomic data to help turn genomic information into new drugs. (UNVERIFIED)
A spectroscopic database holding mass spectrometry datasets, chiefly from proteomics experiments. It stores the measurements themselves consenting to check reproducibility.

The Spectral Database for Organic Compounds (SDBS) is a free, searchable online database of experimental molecular spectra for organic molecules, hosted by the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) in Japan. SDBS contains NMR (1H, 13C), mass spectra, IR, Raman, and ESR spectra for a large number of organic compounds.

An NMR data repository collecting nuclear magnetic resonance measurements on biological macromolecules and metabolites, including assigned chemical shifts, coupling constants and relaxation data. Those quantities are what a simulated structure or trajectory is compared against.

An NMR data repository specialising in assigned chemical shifts for complex carbohydrates and their complexes. Carbohydrates are poorly covered by the general NMR archives, because their signals overlap heavily and their assignment is difficult. It exists to hold the assignments that do get made. (UNVERIFIED)

A secondary database, run by EMBL-EBI, that combines the protein family, domain and functional site signatures of several member databases, such as Pfam, PROSITE, SMART, CDD and CATH-Gene3D, into 1 resource. Searching a protein sequence against it shows which families and domains the protein belongs to, which helps predict its function. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein family and domain database in which each family is represented by a multiple sequence alignment and a hidden Markov model, a statistical model of the sequence pattern the family shares. It is used to find conserved domains and families in protein sequences, and it is now provided through InterPro at EMBL-EBI. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein family and domain database for identifying and annotating mobile domains, which are domains found in many different protein contexts, and for analysing the domain architecture of proteins. It is developed at EMBL and holds manually curated models for more than 1,000 domains, many of them involved in signalling, extracellular functions and chromatin regulation. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein family and domain database that describes protein domains, families and functional sites by sequence patterns or by profiles, which are scoring tables derived from multiple sequence alignments. It is maintained by the SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics and is used to find known motifs and domains in a protein sequence. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein family and domain database, maintained by NCBI, holding curated models of protein domains together with models imported from other collections, such as Pfam and SMART. Searching a sequence against it shows which known domains a protein contains, which helps decide what part of a protein to simulate. (UNVERIFIED)

A structural classification database that classifies protein domains of known structure by their evolutionary relationships and structural similarities. It is the successor of the original SCOP, developed at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, and organises its classes as a network in which a domain can be related to more than 1 group, instead of the single strict tree that SCOP used. (UNVERIFIED)

A structural classification database that sorts protein domains taken from experimental structures into a hierarchy of 4 levels, from broad shape down to evolutionary relationship. The 4 levels are what its name enumerates. It is used to find structurally similar proteins when sequence similarity is too weak to detect. (UNVERIFIED)

A structural classification database that groups protein domains by evolutionary relationship rather than by shape, with a focus on distant relationships between proteins whose sequences have become too different to show them. Its levels run from architecture through possible homology (X-groups), homology (H-groups) and topology (T-groups) to families, and it is updated regularly as new structures enter the Protein Data Bank. (UNVERIFIED)

A pathway database of manually drawn maps of molecular interaction and reaction networks, covering metabolism, genetic and environmental information processing, cellular processes, organismal systems and human diseases. It is part of the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), developed in Japan by Kanehisa Laboratories. (UNVERIFIED)

A pathway database of human biological pathways and processes that is free, open-source, curated by experts and peer-reviewed. It describes biology as a hierarchy running from single molecular reactions up to whole pathways, linking the genes, proteins and small molecules involved. (UNVERIFIED)

A pathway database that collects thousands of organism-specific databases, each describing the genome and metabolic pathways of 1 organism, together with MetaCyc, a reference database of pathways from many organisms. It is maintained by SRI International and records genes, enzymes, metabolites and reactions, which supports the comparison of metabolism between organisms. (UNVERIFIED)

A pathway database of biological pathway diagrams that anyone can contribute to and edit, so the collection is curated by its community of users. It covers many species, and its content is released under the CC0 public domain waiver. (UNVERIFIED)

A public, web-accessible database focusing on measured binding affinities of interactions between proteins (considered as drug targets) and small, drug-like molecules. It primarily contains data from enzyme assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, and surface plasmon resonance.

A free, public repository hosted by the U.S. National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) that archives experimental descriptions of biological activities and test results for small molecules, cell-based screens, and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs).

An expert-curated, open-access online portal and searchable database that provides quantitative data on biological targets and the prescription medicines and experimental drugs that act on them. Its entries are written and checked by specialists in each target family rather than gathered automatically.

A knowledge-based database that collects gene-disease and variant-disease associations from public databases and the scientific literature, standardises them, and scores each association so that it can be ranked. It is developed by the company MedBioinformatics Solutions, with free access for academic research and paid licences for commercial use. (UNVERIFIED)

A knowledge-based database cataloguing human genes and the inherited disorders and traits associated with them. It is organised around the link between a gene and the effects of altering it, rather than around sequences. It can be used to connect a mutation being simulated to its known clinical consequences. (UNVERIFIED)

A repository database for research outputs from all disciplines, such as datasets, software, publications and figures, operated by CERN and created within the European OpenAIRE project. Every upload receives a DOI, a permanent identifier that makes it citable. (UNVERIFIED)

A repository database, checked by curators, that publishes the data underlying scientific and medical publications so that the data can be found, freely reused and cited. Researchers deposit the datasets that belong to their articles, and the data are released into the public domain under the CC0 dedication. (UNVERIFIED)

A repository database where researchers in any discipline can store and share research outputs such as figures, datasets, images and code. Each item can be given a DOI, a permanent identifier that makes it citable and easier to find. (UNVERIFIED)

A simulation data repository, based in Europe, for storing and sharing biomolecular simulation data. It accepts trajectories together with the metadata describing how they were produced, which is what makes a deposited trajectory reusable by others. (UNVERIFIED)

A simulation data repository for molecular dynamics trajectories of biomolecules, contributed by the biomolecular simulation community in the United Kingdom and hosted by the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI). It records how each simulation was set up, from the starting structure and force field to the run parameters, so that the data can be reproduced and reused. (UNVERIFIED)

A simulation data repository of atomistic molecular dynamics trajectories of proteins, chosen to represent the monomeric soluble protein structures in the Protein Data Bank. It was developed by IRB Barcelona and the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, and its trajectories are used to describe how flexible each protein is. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: Distinct from the class 'model' (MOLSIM:000006), which it resembles only in spelling: this is a named simulation data repository, that is a general kind of representation. Case-insensitive lexical matching conflates the two, so prefer the synonym 'MoDEL database' when matching.

definition.val: A web server tool for sharing, viewing and analysing molecular dynamics simulation trajectories directly in a web browser, without installing software locally. A research group runs it on its own server to make its trajectories available to others, with interactive views and common analyses. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein structural database for structures of biological molecules determined by integrative or hybrid methods, which combine data from several experimental techniques with computational modelling. It began as a prototype archive and in 2024 was unified with the Protein Data Bank and renamed PDB-IHM, so its structures now receive PDB accession codes. (UNVERIFIED)

A predicted structure repository that gives open access to protein structure predictions made by the AlphaFold system, covering a large share of the protein sequences in UniProt. It is run by EMBL-EBI together with Google DeepMind, and supplies models for proteins that have no experimentally determined structure. (UNVERIFIED)

A predicted structure repository of 3D protein models built automatically by the SWISS-MODEL homology modelling pipeline, which bases each model on an experimentally determined structure of a related protein. It is updated regularly and provides precomputed models for a large number of sequences in UniProtKB, especially those of model organisms. (UNVERIFIED)

A predicted structure repository holding several hundred million structure predictions for metagenomic proteins, which are proteins known only from DNA sequenced directly from environmental samples, made with the ESMFold model developed at Meta AI. ESMFold predicts a structure from a single sequence with a protein language model, without first collecting related sequences, which makes it much faster than earlier methods but on average less accurate. (UNVERIFIED)

A predicted structure repository for 3D models of biological macromolecules made by computational methods, which the Protein Data Bank does not accept because they are not based on experimental data. Each deposited model receives a stable accession code, which is also a DOI, so that it can be cited, and the archive is developed by the SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics and the Biozentrum of the University of Basel. (UNVERIFIED)

A metabolomics repository, maintained at EMBL-EBI, for metabolomics experiments across species and measurement techniques, together with the information derived from them. It archives study descriptions, raw experimental data and the identified and measured metabolites. (UNVERIFIED)

A metabolomics repository and analysis platform for mass spectrometry data on natural products, which groups related compounds by the similarity of their spectra. Grouping this way helps suggest the identity of compounds that no reference library contains, from their resemblance to ones that it does. Its reference spectra are contributed and curated by its users. (UNVERIFIED)

synonyms.val: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking

definition.val: A public repository for metabolomics data and metadata, part of the NIH Common Fund's Metabolomics Program. It serves as a national and international data repository and coordinating center, providing tools for data analysis, visualization, and integration with other omics data. (UNVERIFIED)

A literature database, run by the U.S. National Library of Medicine at the National Institutes of Health, that gives free search access to references and abstracts in the life sciences and biomedicine, drawn mainly from the MEDLINE database. Its records link to the full text where a publisher or PubMed Central makes it available. (UNVERIFIED)

A literature database of abstracts and citations covering peer-reviewed journals, books and conference proceedings, owned by the publisher Elsevier and available by subscription. It provides tools to track, analyse and visualise research output and citations across disciplines. (UNVERIFIED)

A literature database and citation index covering many disciplines, owned by the company Clarivate and available by subscription. It gives access to several databases of scholarly journals, books, conference proceedings and patents, with the citation links between their records, and is used for literature searches and for measuring research impact. (UNVERIFIED)

A literature database, provided free of charge by Google as a web search engine, that indexes the full text or metadata of scholarly literature across many publishing formats and disciplines. It is not curated: its index is built automatically, so its coverage is broad but its records can contain errors. (UNVERIFIED)

The small molecule structural database that serves as the primary repository for experimentally determined three-dimensional crystal structures of small organic and metal-organic molecules. It provides high-quality reference geometries used for validating force fields and for obtaining starting structures in computational studies. (UNVERIFIED)
OBSOLETE. A redundant untyped individual that duplicated the class 'omni-path' (MOLSIM:001949). It should not be used; use that class instead.

comments: Obsoleted: redundant untyped individual duplicating the class 'omni-path' (MOLSIM_001949), which is the concept to use instead.

definition.val: The file format convention denoted by the string AMBERRESTART in a NetCDF file's global Conventions attribute, designating the file as an AMBER restart or state file. Such a file holds a single configuration with no frame dimension, while a trajectory holds many frames, and because NetCDF is a general container this attribute is the declared way to tell the 2 apart. (UNVERIFIED)

The file format convention denoted by the string AMBER in a NetCDF file's global Conventions attribute, designating the file as an AMBER coordinate trajectory. It is the counterpart of the restart convention and distinguishes a file of many frames from a file holding 1 state. The distinction cannot be made from the file extension alone. (UNVERIFIED)

The system classification label assigned to a molecular system composed of a protein receptor, a small-molecule ligand and explicit water molecules. Explicit water means that individual water molecules are present in the model, rather than a continuum that only imitates their average effect. (UNVERIFIED)

The hydrogen detection strategy that identifies hydrogen atoms by testing whether an atom's atomic number is exactly 1, used when applying or detecting hydrogen mass repartitioning. It is the reliable test, because atomic number is a physical fact recorded in the topology. It cannot be used where the topology omits atomic numbers, which is why a name-based fallback exists. (UNVERIFIED)

The hydrogen detection strategy that identifies hydrogen atoms by testing whether an atom's name begins with the letter H, used when applying or detecting hydrogen mass repartitioning. It is a fallback for topologies that do not record atomic numbers. It is not reliable: the element symbols of helium, hafnium and mercury (He, Hf, Hg) also begin with H, and some naming conventions put a digit before the H. (UNVERIFIED)
The term was added to the ontology on the assumption it was in scope, but it turned out later that it was not.
The term was added to the ontology on the assumption it was a valid domain entity, but it turns out the entity does not exist in reality.
The concise, meaningful, and human-friendly name for a class or property preferred by the ontology developers. (US-English)

A phrase describing how a term should be used and/or a citation to a work which uses it. May also include other kinds of examples that facilitate immediate understanding, such as widely know prototypes or instances of a class, or cases where a relation is said to hold.
The official definition, explaining the meaning of a class or property. Shall be Aristotelian, formalized and normalized. Can be augmented with colloquial definitions.

basicPropertyValues.val:
2012-04-05: 
Barry Smith

The official OBI definition, explaining the meaning of a class or property: 'Shall be Aristotelian, formalized and normalized. Can be augmented with colloquial definitions'  is terrible.

Can you fix to something like:

A statement of necessary and sufficient conditions explaining the meaning of an expression referring to a class or property.

Alan Ruttenberg

Your proposed definition is a reasonable candidate, except that it is very common that necessary and sufficient conditions are not given. Mostly they are necessary, occasionally they are necessary and sufficient or just sufficient. Often they use terms that are not themselves defined and so they effectively can't be evaluated by those criteria. 

On the specifics of the proposed definition:

We don't have definitions of 'meaning' or 'expression' or 'property'. For 'reference' in the intended sense I think we use the term 'denotation'. For 'expression', I think we you mean symbol, or identifier. For 'meaning' it differs for class and property. For class we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine whether an entity is instance of the class, or not. For property we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine, given a pair of potential relata, whether the assertion that the relation holds is true. The 'intended reader' part suggests that we also specify who, we expect, would be able to understand the definition, and also generalizes over human and computer reader to include textual and logical definition. 

Personally, I am more comfortable weakening definition to documentation, with instructions as to what is desirable. 

We also have the outstanding issue of how to aim different definitions to different audiences. A clinical audience reading chebi wants a different sort of definition documentation/definition from a chemistry trained audience, and similarly there is a need for a definition that is adequate for an ontologist to work with.

definition.val: An administrative note intended for its editor. It may not be included in the publication version of the ontology, so it should contain nothing necessary for end users to understand the ontology.

Name of editor entering the term in the file. The term editor is a point of contact for information regarding the term. The term editor may be, but is not always, the author of the definition, which may have been worked upon by several people

The program the name belongs to is recorded as the source of each such statement, so 1 property serves every program. (UNVERIFIED)
